```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(nflfastR)
library(nflplotR)
library(purrr)
library(mgcv)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Tracking Data
full_df <- read_csv("~/Documents/Football_R/CMSAC--Field Value/full_data.csv")
field_control <- read.csv("~/Documents/Football_R/CMSAC--Field Value/field_control_data.csv")

#Field Value Model
field_value <- readRDS("~/Documents/Football_R/CMSAC--Field Value/gam_field_value_model.rds")
```

```{r}
play_data <- full_df %>% 
  select(game_id, play_id, frame_id, ball_land_y_std, expected_points, los_x_std, dropback_distance) %>% 
  distinct()

feed_model <- field_control %>% 
  left_join(play_data, by = c("game_id", "frame_id", "play_id")) %>% 
  mutate(pass_depth = x - los_x_std) %>% 
  # Eliminate impossible passes that land beyond the back of the endzone (110 yards)
  filter((los_x_std + pass_depth) <= 110)

# Assuming your big dataset is loaded, or you are reading it in chunks
chunk_size <- 1000000  # Process 1 million rows at a time
total_rows <- nrow(feed_model)
predictions_list <- list()

for (i in seq(1, total_rows, by = chunk_size)) {
  
  # Define start and end of chunk
  start_row <- i
  end_row <- min(i + chunk_size - 1, total_rows)
  
  # Subset the data
  chunk <- feed_model[start_row:end_row, ]
  
  # Predict and store in the list
  cat("Predicting rows", start_row, "to", end_row, "\n")
  predictions_list[[length(predictions_list) + 1]] <- predict(field_value, newdata = chunk)
  
  # Free up memory
  rm(chunk)
  gc() # Force garbage collection
}

# Combine all predictions back together, compute point efficiency
feed_model$pred_post_epa <- unlist(predictions_list)
feed_model$epa <-  feed_model$pred_post_epa - feed_model$expected_points
feed_model$efficiency <- feed_model$epa * feed_model$ppcf_att
all_efficiency <- feed_model %>% 
  mutate(efficiency = ifelse((pass_depth - dropback_distance) <= 0, 0, efficiency)) %>% 
  group_by(game_id, play_id) %>% 
  summarize(
    coverage_efficiency = mean(efficiency),
    throw_frame = first(frame_id), 
    pass_depth = first(pass_depth)
  )

write.csv(feed_model, "grid_coverage_efficiency.csv")
write.csv(all_efficiency, "pbp_coverage_efficiency.csv")
```

```{r}
single_play <- feed_model %>% 
  filter(game_id == 2023090700, play_id == 461)

plays_list <- full_df %>%
  filter(game_id == 2023090700, play_id == 461)

extract_player_data <- function(play_data) {
  
  # Filter and mutate to create the clean player_data dataframe
  player_data <- play_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(nfl_id), phase == "pre_pass") %>%
    mutate(
      player_side = tolower(player_side), 
      dir_rad = dir_std * pi / 180, 
      vx = s * sin(dir_rad),
      vy = s * cos(dir_rad)
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(x_std) & !is.na(y_std) & !is.na(vx) & !is.na(vy))
  
  # Return NULL if the resulting dataframe is empty
  if (nrow(player_data) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  return(player_data)
}

# 2. Define the static plotting function
plot_nfl_efficiency_static <- function(surface_data, player_data) {
  
  # Filter out NAs based on the standardized coordinate names
  player_data <- player_data %>%
    mutate(player_side = tolower(player_side)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(x_std) & !is.na(y_std) & !is.na(vx) & !is.na(vy))
  
  ymin <- 0; ymax <- 53.3
  xmin <- 0; xmax <- 120
  
  field_plot <- ggplot() +
    annotate("rect", xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = "#1e7a3a") +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 10, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = "#135c29") +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 110, xmax = 120, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = "#135c29") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = seq(10, 110, by = 5), color = "white", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = seq(10, 110, by = 10), color = "white", linewidth = 1)
  
  static_plot <- field_plot +
    
    # Efficiency tile surface
    geom_tile(
      data = surface_data, 
      aes(x = x, y = y, fill = efficiency), 
      alpha = 0.65
    ) +
    # Updated color scale to handle efficiency's negative and positive range
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "#1e40af", mid = "white", high = "#b91c1c", 
      midpoint = 0, 
      name = "Efficiency"
    ) +
    
    # Velocity Vectors 
    geom_segment(
      data = player_data,
      aes(
        x = x_std, y = y_std, 
        xend = x_std + vx * 0.5, yend = y_std + vy * 0.5,
        color = player_side
      ),
      arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "cm")), 
      linewidth = 0.8 
    ) +
    
    # Black borders for player dots 
    geom_point(
      data = player_data, 
      aes(x = x_std, y = y_std), 
      size = 4, color = "black"
    ) +
    
    # Colored inside for player dots 
    geom_point(
      data = player_data, 
      aes(x = x_std, y = y_std, color = player_side), 
      size = 2.8 
    ) +
    
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("offense" = "#facc15", "defense" = "#3b82f6"),
      name = "Team"
    ) +
    
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    ) +
    
    labs(title = 'Play Efficiency Surface')
  
  return(static_plot)
}

# =============================================================================
# --- RENDER ---
# =============================================================================

# NOTE: You must provide a valid `player_data` dataframe from your environment
# for the players to render on the field.

static_plot <- plot_nfl_efficiency_static(surface_data = single_play, player_data = extract_player_data(plays_list))
print(static_plot)
```
